headline: An engineer says OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model cracked the code of a secret 1809 letter written at Napoleon's request, in about six hours.
score_reason: The news is from 30 Sep 2026 and rests on the engineer's own account, though an independent cryptographer confirmed the solution.
importance_line: Historians and codebreakers may gain a faster way to read old coded letters, but the AI started from a partial key that already existed, the engineer himself says the code was not especially hard, and one historian says the text adds little that was not known.
summary: Live Science reports that Carter Church, an AI engineer at the security firm Sentinel One, says he gave OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model one prompt and one low-resolution scan, and it worked out the secret code in the letter, with a cryptographer who tracks unsolved ciphers confirming the solution. One historian quoted says the translation is believable but adds little new, because Napoleon's own letter already described what the message should say.
notes: Church posted on 30 Sep 2026; Live Science article dated 2 Oct 2026. Score lowered 5 to 4 (stale by two days).
